title: Base 16: exact downward bonds at every across-count; sharp unrestricted bound partial
claim: For every n >= 3 and k >= 2 the downward support of floor((n+1)/2)+3 distinctions is a bond of the infinite base, with exactly two complementary assignments excluded. Every induced rectangle with at least three across-counts extends exactly to the infinite base. The sharp unrestricted across-count lower bound is not established here.
standard_statement: For every n >= 3 and k >= 2 the downward support of floor((n+1)/2)+3 distinctions is a bond of the infinite base, with exactly two complementary assignments excluded. Every induced rectangle with at least three across-counts extends exactly to the infinite base. The sharp unrestricted across-count lower bound is not established here.
prior_work: ACROSS-FOLD proves upward heddles and a lower bound for one supporting along-count. Its downward family was finite at y=-3 through -10, k=5,8,11,20. This family proves the full downward projection for every n>=3,k>=2, by a two-update extension; mixed-support optimality is left open.
completion_gate: Prove the unrestricted lower bound for the claimed range, or verify a strict counterexample on the infinite base with allowed-state and deletion witnesses. If only a partial result is reached, establish a rigorous new subfamily or obstruction and present the exact missing step. Cover both signs where justified.

validation.status: hand proof with exact SAT projections, explicit infinite-extension constructors, two finite encodings, K1-K3 and matched rejected overstatements
validation.uniform_theorems: argued-in-prose; finite replay is a consistency check

remaining_obligations: Prove the sharp across-count lower bound for arbitrary finite supports at arbitrary along-counts, or exhibit a strict smaller bond in the far-along-count regime. Do not infer that lower bound from finite negative boxes.
terminal_disposition: Closed Partial for the sharp across-count lower bound. The exact downward upper construction and the finite-rectangle extension theorem are accepted. The coefficient for unrestricted supports remains open.
